newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Heavy security at strike-hit Rusplats mine. [CORRECTED 13:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Heavy security at strike-hit Rusplats mine. [CORRECTED 13:52 GMT]

text.p: A heavy security and police contingent was deployed at South Africa's strike-hit Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd on Wednesday but the situation was calm, a company spokesman said.

Negotiations to end the wildcat strike by two-thirds of the workforce at the Amandelbult section of the world's biggest platinum mine were continuing but there were no immediate signs of a breakthrough.
The strike is affecting 15-20 percent of total Rusplats output.

The 4,600 workers from two of the three Amandelbult hostels who went on strike on Monday night again failed to turn up for the afternoon shift, due to start at 2.00 p.m. (1200 GMT), the spokesman said.
The remaining third of the workforce went down the mine as normal.
"It's calm and quiet at the mine," the spokesman told Reuters from the site 120 km northwest of Johannesburg.
"There is a strong security and police presence to assist those who wish to go down to work."
The spokesman added that the appeal case for a suspended employee dismissed on Friday for alleged clocking fraud was being heard on Wednesday afternoon.
His sacking triggered the latest unrest and clashes.
Rusplats produced 690,000 ounces of platinum in the six months to December 31, 1996, equivalent to around a quarter of world supply.
In the financial year to June 30, 1996 it produced 698,000 oz of palladium, 149,700 oz of rhodium and 14,100 tonnes of nickel.
(Corrects from 14.1 tonnes of nickel). Platinum production in the same period was 1.553 million oz.
